subject: Fresh Foundation payload compilation and scalar execution
claim: The selected 371-case checkpoint compiles record/u32 and allocated-text borrow fixtures twice with identical WVB 1.39 bytes and executes both with result 42 on Windows. Debian completed its component checks and rebuilt three matching compiler-support modules, but fresh candidate publication/execution remains incomplete after a deliberate setup-budget stop.

source.value: Worktree based on d3fe034fd6014464fd338e0bf3eca587e7b7f471. Only the retained verifier, its registry count, the new text fixture, and documentation change; compiler/runtime sources and runner packages are unchanged.

runs.target: 371 selected Foundation groups; fresh deterministic record/u32 and allocated-text publication and execution
Focused Foundation source-to-runtime checkpoint, stopped during current analyzer packaging after approximately 23 minutes
Verifier routing and retained owner registry: 31 general and 291 native cases; six front-end products and 63 subsets

limitations: The text fixture checks Option absence, both unselected Result projections, allocated selected text, borrowed helper forwarding, and eight calls with fresh frame-local owners. It is not a full-arena lifetime stress test or a maintained real consumer.

The initial text fixture used nonexistent Textˉlength and failed source analysis with Invalidˉargument. It was corrected to the implemented Bytesˉlength(Textˉtoˉutf8(Value)); no compiler implementation change was needed.
The Windows timing uses warm construction caches. It is not a cold-build performance claim; peak working-set memory was not measured.

Debian cold pinned analyzer/emitter packaging took 461365/311179 ms. Current admitter/validator/analyzer WVB construction took 77277/8574/321016 ms; admitter/validator packaging took 127997/13372 ms. These completed products were cached. The remaining analyzer packaging plus emitter construction and packaging could no longer reasonably fit the 1800-second allowance. The owned staging process group was deliberately terminated with SIGTERM; the wrapper exited 1 and cleaned its temporary work. This is incomplete evidence, not an assertion failure or a passing Debian checkpoint.

The next Debian work should select the remaining native compiler construction products with an explicit measured budget, then reuse valid products for focused publication/execution. Do not blindly retry the cold pipeline or report the unexecuted 371 groups as passed.
The runner packages are reused from the preceding runtime checkpoint, built from one Windows-produced runner WVB. This is not independent compiler/bootstrap reconstruction.

Temporary candidate outputs are removed by the existing verifier cleanup after their byte identities and results are checked. The record/u32 output also matches the previously published pinned candidate.

The retained full owner includes the new text determinism case and two fresh executions, raising its registered total from 549 to 552. The full 552-case owner was not run. The no-runner publication selection remains 368 groups and does not claim execution.

The changed-file plan selected the broad front-door and memory-budget owners with 1230 expected seconds. The focused 371-group publication/execution selection directly covers the new fixture's source admission, analysis, emission, and runtime behavior; unrelated full front-door, task, callable, browser, installed-tool, OS, ABI, and complete qualification suites were not run.

Existing portable, synchronous, capability-free host execution limits remain unchanged. Arbitrary payload execution, exclusive borrowing, take, mapping, maintained-consumer migration, native WVB 1.39 lowering, installed-tool promotion, and overall compiler/library completion remain open.
